name: Broad-spectrum sunscreen

lead: Broad-spectrum sunscreen is a topical product containing filters that block both UVB and UVA radiation. It comes as lotions, gels, sticks and sprays in chemical, mineral and hybrid forms.
It is the product with the strongest evidence base for anti-aging and skin-cancer prevention among skincare products, and dermatologists regularly recommend it.

paras: Filters absorb UV photons (chemical filters) or reflect and scatter them (mineral filters such as zinc oxide and titanium dioxide), reducing the dose that reaches the skin. The Nambour randomized trial of 903 adults found daily sunscreen users had about 24 percent less skin aging over 4.5 years than discretionary users.

Protection depends on applying enough and reapplying; most people under-apply. Irritation and allergic reactions occur, and some people dislike the white cast of mineral products. Environmental concerns about some filters are debated. Evidence supports sunscreen as reducing photoaging; it does not make high-risk sun exposure safe.
